Messages.Author: KevinM
Messages.Body:
Here are a few underrated cards that I have used to great effectiveness:

Gather - Most people never take the action to get rid of it, which usually means a "free" minion for you, and since it's a Gangrel card, it it usually followed by a Freak Drive, which means it was a "free" action. You can also do the Gather-House of Sorrow trick, if you're so inclined.

Arson - It's free, and the all-purpose, non-limited usage is incredibly powerful, especially if a particular location is going to be a bother to your deck.

Police Department - It's free, it doesn't have a removal clause, and it stops the presses that are likely to kill your minions.

Charming Lobby - It's free, gives you +2 votes to do what your deck does anyway, and gives a lingering effect to allow you to force through those highly unlikeable votes.

Underbridge Stray - It's a cheap ally that can block, it provides a permanent untap(!), and similarly to Police Department, it provides a press (either way), which can often save you, or help kill your enemies.

Veles' Hunt - This is only really played in one deck, but in that deck, it's PTO. Note that PTO has been banned...

Jackie Therman - She's free, and to decks that can't via their disciplines, she provides a much-needed maneuver. And use the VTES hot-redhead version, will you?

Last Stand - While people are continually trying to get Momentum's Edge to work, and asking themselves why it doesn't work, I'm winning games with Last Stand. No other card in the game allows you to do what this does. It's ridiculously powerful and should be in every power-bleed deck.

The Bitter and Sweet Story - Another powerful card that should be in every power-bleed deck. You're going to get 1vp. That's just a fact. And when you get it, you'll get a 29% increase in your hand size, which will allow you to get out of hand-jam situations MUCH easier. And it doesn't matter that it's a global effect, because no deck is rewarded for a larger hand size than a bleed deck is.

Psychic Veil - I've played 1-2 of these in every obfuscate deck since the olden days and it's always been amazing. At [obf], it's for all your vampires, and given how many weenie-obf decks are out there, 1 blood for +4, +5, or +6 stealth is pretty damn good.

Messages.Author: Azel
Messages.Body:
Perhaps not the most underrated cards, let alone powerful, but I'm partial to Status Perfectus, Meat Hook, Bloodstone, and Ghoul Messenger. They're pretty well overlooked in my experience, however.

Status Perfectus helps with blood management, and has on more than one occasion prevented a mandatory empty hunt with a minion who wouldn't be able to get it through. At the end game those desperate lunges and forced hunts can mean VPs or being exposed for the oust.

Meat Hook is a permanent superior Mighty Grapple with a semi-trap option for vampires w/ potence to waste a strike -- and it works with melee strike cards, too. Cheap grinder hitback. Also Concealable. Nice for non-add-strike decks.

Bloodstone is a finesse card which I've received the most colorful post-game comments. I've had players talk about how upset they were with that little equipment getting in the way. Hey, if it buys me time, how bad can it be? Also useful in "assisting" that S&B grand-predator flush out their stealth on your predator; keeps you alive, they run low eventually... Even weenie support moving the Bloodstone equipment away stresses minion management issues later. An unfairly maligned card, I think.

Ghoul Messenger is the Leather Jacket hunt action for Laibon. Even in destruction by being blocked it helps because combat is canceled. A nice way to recoup blood for a turn and stay on the defensive without stressing your wakes.

Not really...the whole "fame dunk" stuff is a myth that's totally not worth the effort.

Torp -> rescue -> Torp is 3 actions to do 6 pool damage. Those actions cost blood and likely cards, unless you happen to have two guys with permarush. And then there's hitback too. While Aranthebes is untapped, vampires with a capacity less than 5 get -1 bleed when bleeding you. Any vampire with a capacity above 4 can move Aranthebes to your library as a  action. Shuffle afterward.

Permanent "intercept" on your predator, the bleed reduction for weenies is just a bonus.

Messages.Author: Chaitan
Messages.Body:
> Victim of Habit
> Type: Action
> Cost: 1 blood
> +1 stealth action.
> Put this card in play and choose a card in your prey's ash heap by name. During any Methuselah's untap phase, you may tap this card to remove three copies of the chosen card in your prey's ash heap from the game to cause your prey to burn 1 pool.
>
Its strength increases against decks that cycle cards fast (which is often a good measure of a good deck).

It is good against ash heap digging decks.

Playable by any vampire. So your little cap 2 can do it.

Its real strength is punishing deck types that is designed around a single card and those can be troublesome to beat.

It is not unique so you can even have multiple copies out.

In any game you can expect to deal atleast 1-2 pool damage to prey. It may not be much but depending on prey (or if you choose a common card, perhaps even next prey) this can be alot more.
